title: Juniper and the Orbit
premise: Orsen Eriksen is a licensed clone of a murdered detective, running cargo on the Juniper along the silent corridor between the Meridian and Halcyon fleets—two armadas that stopped speaking after the war that killed her original. When she intercepts a distress call in Old Meridian Sign-Speech, a language only clones of the dead are trained to read, she realizes the sender is another clone hiding among Halcyon's crew, and that both fleets are being manipulated toward a final battle timed to the jump window. To stop it, Orsen must impersonate her dead original convincingly enough to broker peace between fleets that believe she died with him—while concealing from everyone, including herself, whether she is a person or just his echo. In the end she broadcasts the truth of her own identity alongside the forged 'last orders' of Eriksen Prime, holding the lie and the truth together long enough for the fleets to stand down as the window closes.
about_author: Gideon Kavanagh is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships whose owners no longer spoke to each other. They write science fiction about people who carry other people's words.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Orsen pilots the Juniper through the demilitarized corridor between the Meridian and Halcyon fleets, establishing her routine of silence, forged manifests, and careful invisibility. Flashbacks reveal she inherited her original's memories—and his unsolved murder case—under clone law. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the comfort of being no one.

chapters.title: A Voice in Dead Language
chapters.summary: A distress signal arrives in Old Meridian Sign-Speech, extinct since the Fleet Schism; only legacy-trained clones like Orsen can parse it. The transmission is fragmented but human, and it names her original's case number. She must choose: log it and stay invisible, or answer. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the pull of duty she never asked to inherit.

chapters.title: What the Clone Remembers
chapters.summary: Orsen answers covertly and traces the signal to the Halcyon tender Vespergate. Interrogating her inherited memories, she reconstructs Eriksen Prime's final investigation—a conspiracy inside Meridian command to provoke a fleet war. POV: Orsen, with memory-sequences in Eriksen Prime's voice. Emotional beat: grief braided with suspicion about whose feelings these really are.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't Issued
chapters.summary: Boarding Vespergate under a maintenance pretext, Orsen meets Sefa Ilo, the signal's sender—another clone, grown from a murdered Meridian linguist and passed off as crew. Sefa has proof of the provocation plot but no way to deliver it across the silent corridor. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: recognition—the first person who understands what she is.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Sefa reveals the jump window: in eleven days both fleets transit the same corridor node, and planted evidence will make each believe the other fired first. Orsen proposes an audacious plan—she will impersonate Eriksen Prime, whose 'posthumous testimony' both fleets still legally recognize, to force a parley. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: terror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Dead
chapters.summary: Orsen drills Sefa in Eriksen Prime's mannerisms while wrestling with the ethics: to save thousands she must convince two fleets that a dead man lives, erasing her own selfhood in the performance. A Meridian patrol nearly boards the Juniper. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: identity fraying at the seams—where does the act end?

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Broadcasting as Eriksen Prime from the corridor relay, Orsen presents the murder case file and demands a neutral parley at the node before the window closes. Meridian command accepts—but dispatches an investigator who knew the original intimately. POV: Orsen, intercut with fleet command channels. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by imminent exposure.

chapters.title: Someone Who Knew His Face
chapters.summary: Investigator Dara Voss boards the Juniper and begins dismantling the impersonation with personal questions no memory-file can fully answer. Orsen survives by answering as herself instead of as him—an honesty Voss finds more convincing than any forgery. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: the discovery that truth is a better disguise than the lie.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: The provocation plotters, exposed by Voss's defection, jam the parley and launch the false attack early. With minutes before the jump window seals, Orsen makes her choice: she drops the impersonation entirely and broadcasts in her own voice, as a clone, claiming the case—and the ceasefire—as hers. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: climax—self-annihilation refused, identity claimed under fire.

chapters.title: Juniper, Standing By
chapters.summary: Both fleets hold fire as the window closes with them safely apart; the conspirators are arrested under the very testimony Orsen authored. Weeks later, the corridor reopens to traffic and letters. Orsen and Sefa run the route together, no longer invisible, no longer anyone else. POV: Orsen. Emotional beat: quiet belonging—justice delivered outside the law, by someone finally real to herself.
